title: Git Merging and Conflict Resolution
description: Learn how to combine changes from different branches and resolve conflicts

steps.title: Understanding Merging
steps.content:
Merging combines changes from different branches:

Types of merges:
- Fast-forward: When target branch is direct descendant
- Recursive: When branches have diverged
- Squash: Combine all changes into one commit

Key concepts:
- Common ancestor: Point where branches diverged
- Merge base: Reference point for combining changes
- Merge commit: Special commit with multiple parents
- Clean working directory: Required for merging

steps.title: Basic Merging
steps.content:
Steps to merge a feature branch:

1. Ensure working directory is clean (git status)
2. Switch to target branch: git checkout main
3. Merge source branch: git merge feature-branch
4. Push merged changes: git push

Common merge flags:
- --no-ff: Create merge commit even for fast-forward
- --squash: Combine all changes into one commit
- --abort: Cancel problematic merge

practical_task.description: Create a feature branch, make changes, then merge it back to main. Type 'done' when complete.

steps.title: Handling Merge Conflicts
steps.content:
Conflicts occur when same lines change in both branches:

Conflict markers in files:
<<<<<<< HEAD
Your changes in current branch
=======
Incoming changes from other branch
>>>>>>> feature-branch

Steps to resolve:
1. Open conflicted files
2. Choose desired changes
3. Remove conflict markers
4. git add resolved files
5. git commit to complete merge

practical_task.description: Create and resolve a merge conflict by changing the same line in two branches. Type 'done' when resolved.

steps.title: Advanced Merging Strategies
steps.content:
Different approaches to merging:

Merge Strategies:
- ours: Keep our version of conflicting changes
- theirs: Keep their version of conflicting changes
- octopus: Merge multiple branches at once

Tools and Commands:
- git mergetool: Launch visual merge tool
- git diff: Compare branches before merge
- git log --graph: Visualize branch history

Best Practices:
- Keep commits small and focused
- Merge frequently to reduce conflicts
- Write clear commit messages
- Review changes before merging
- Test after resolving conflicts

practical_task.description: Use git log --graph to visualize your branch history. What command shows a compact version?

exercises.question: What is a fast-forward merge?
exercises.explanation: A fast-forward merge occurs when the target branch is a direct descendant of the source branch, allowing Git to simply move the pointer forward.

exercises.question: What command merges a feature branch into main?
exercises.explanation: Use git merge <branch-name> to merge changes from the specified branch into your current branch.

exercises.question: What should you do after resolving merge conflicts?
exercises.explanation: After resolving conflicts, use git add to stage the resolved files, then git commit to complete the merge.

exercises.question: What command aborts a problematic merge?
exercises.explanation: git merge --abort cancels the current merge operation and returns the repository to its pre-merge state.
